edition.name: Migne PL 4 (1844), Ep. LXIV, via Corpus Corporum / Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Lapsi vero magnitudinem delicti sui cognoscentes, a deprecando Domino non recedant, nec Ecclesiam catholicam, quae una et sola est a Domino constituta, derelinquant; sed, satisfactionibus immorantes et Domini misericordiam deprecantes, ad Ecclesiam pulsent, ut recipi illic possint ubi fuerunt, et ad Christum redeant, a quo recesserunt. Nec audiant eos qui se fallaci et mortali seductione decipiunt, cum scriptum sit: Nemo vos decipiat inanibus verbis. Propterea enim venit ira Dei super filios contumaciae. Nolite ergo esse participes eorum. Ergo contumaces et Deum non timentes et ab Ecclesia in totum recedentes nemo comitetur. Quod si quis impatiens fuerit ad deprecandum Dominum qui offensus est, et nobis obtemperare noluerit, sed desperatos et perditos secutus fuerit, sibi imputabit cum judicii dies venerit. Quomodo enim deprecari in die illo Dominum poterit qui et ante hoc Christum et nunc quoque Ecclesiam Christi negavit et, episcopis sanis et integris et viventibus non obtemperans, comitem se et participem morientibus praebuit? Opto vos, fratres charissimi ac desiderantissimi, semper bene valere.
pass_a_gloss: But the lapsed, knowing the magnitude of their own offense, should not withdraw from beseeching the Lord, nor should they abandon the Catholic Church, which is one and alone established by the Lord; but, lingering in satisfactions and beseeching the Lord's mercy, they should knock at the Church so that they may be received there where they were before, and return to Christ, from whom they withdrew. And let them not listen to those who deceive themselves with fallacious and mortal seduction, since it is written: No one should deceive you with empty words. For therefore the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. Do not be sharers of theirs. Therefore, let no one associate with the disobedient and those who do not fear God and totally withdraw from the Church. But if someone is impatient in beseeching the Lord who is offended, and does not want to obey us, but has followed the desperate and the lost, he will impute it to himself when the day of judgment comes. For how will he be able to beseech the Lord on that day, he who both before denied Christ and now also denies the Church of Christ, and, not obeying the healthy and intact and living bishops, has provided himself as a companion and sharer to the dying? I wish you, most dear and desired brothers, to always be well.

bible_refs.note: No one should deceive you with empty words

pass_b_english: The lapsed, recognizing the magnitude of their offense, must not stop beseeching the Lord, nor abandon the Catholic Church, which is the one and only Church established by the Lord. Instead, they should persist in acts of satisfaction and plead for the Lord's mercy; they must knock at the Church so that they may be received back where they once stood, and return to Christ, from whom they have strayed. They must not listen to those who deceive themselves with a fallacious and deadly seduction, for it is written: "Let no one deceive you with empty words." For this reason the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. Do not become partners with them. Therefore no one is to associate with the disobedient, those who do not fear God, and those who withdraw entirely from the Church. But if anyone grows impatient in beseeching the offended Lord and refuses to obey us, choosing instead to follow the desperate and the lost, he will have only himself to blame when the day of judgment arrives. For how will he be able to beseech the Lord on that day, he who denied Christ before and now also denies the Church of Christ? He has refused to obey bishops who are sound, whole, and still alive, making himself a companion and partner to the dying. I pray, my dearest and most longed-for brothers, that you may always fare well.

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both fail to provide the required inline citation for the scripture quote. The Latin text contains 'Nemo vos decipiat inanibus verbis', which is a quotation/allusion. The instructions state: 'match each inline citation to the actual words quoted or alluded to... Added identifications are REQUIRED: never fail the practice, only a wrong verse.' While the notes identify it as Ephesians, the translations themselves lack the required inline parenthetical citation (e.g., Ephesians 5:3 or similar) beside the quoted clause.
reasons: The translations fail to include the required inline parenthetical citation beside the quoted clause 'Nemo vos decipiat inanibus verbis' / 'No one should deceive you with empty words' / 'Let no one deceive you with empty words'.
